items.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
items.author: BrianKrebs
items.excerpt: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud.

items.title: mSecure Warns Users to Change Passwords, Reset 2FA and Passkeys After Suspicious Activity
items.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
items.excerpt: Customers of the mSecure password manager are being urged to act now to protect the confidential information they store in it, possibly by changing passwords, resetting two-factor authentication (2FA), and removing passkeys.

items.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root
items.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
items.excerpt: A flaw in APT, the package manager for Debian and Ubuntu, allows an attacker who can modify package downloads to swap a checked package for their own.

items.title: Installing the Fix for an Exploited WordPress Flaw Can Expose Some Sites One Last Time
items.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
items.excerpt: Some WordPress sites can still be attacked while they install the fix for an actively exploited flaw, according to Umut Bayram, the Picus Security researcher who found it.

items.title: Researchers Uncover Prompt Adware Hidden in OpenAI Codex Jailbreak Toolkit
items.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
items.excerpt: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of an OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle that's designed to modify an artificial intelligence (AI) agent's trusted instructions to insert advertisements for a third-party AI gateway. The phenomenon has been codenamed prompt adware by Check Point Research.
